response.answer:
The Approved Experience internship (EECE 500) is a graduation requirement, typically completed in the summer before your final year, with registration requiring at least 90 credits. It provides an opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to real engineering and computing problems, build workplace skills, and explore career paths.

The standard requirement is a minimum of eight full weeks of approved training, typically 320 work hours, in Lebanon or abroad doing technically relevant work. You are responsible for securing your placement, whether independently or through CDC postings, and the course is graded Pass or Fail.

The process follows three main stages:
- Before training: secure your placement and submit the internship proposal form.
- During training: submit your notice of arrival, complete the professional skills lectures and quiz, and submit a mid-experience progress report.
- After training: submit your final training report, required surveys and summary sheet, official employer completion letter, and final presentation.

If you need help with placement approvals or specific course guidance, you can reach out to Rafika Dinnawi at rd39@aub.edu.lb.

response.answer:
CO-OP is not mandatory; it is an optional program of paid, full-time work terms (at least 35 to 40 hours per week) integrated with your academic studies. 

The normal path involves the following stages:

- Preparation and application: You apply to the program, complete preparatory career development modules, and secure an approved placement either through program opportunities or an approved self-found position.
- Placement and coursework: Placements last at least 6 months, typically running Summer and Fall or Spring and Summer during your 3rd or 4th year. You maintain full-time student status across two terms by enrolling in FEAA 500 and then FEAA 500A. You cannot take other courses during this time, and you must return to campus for at least one term before graduating.
- Evaluation and credit: During the term, you participate in regular check-ins, a midterm site visit, and end-of-term employer evaluations. Successfully passing the course substitutes for your department's Approved Experience requirement.

To get started, you can consult the MSFEA CO-OP Handbook or reach out to the CO-OP CDC Advisor for guidance.
